title: Attenuated token flow allocations for concurrent-route crediting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: when requests traverse multiple routes (canaries, fallbacks, multi-model splits) we currently attribute full token counts to each candidate path during partial attempts which causes over-counting and mis-billing for customers that experience fallbacks or partial retries. This ticket defines and implements an 'attenuated allocation' algorithm so only a weighted fraction of tokens is charged per-attempt, with deterministic reconciliation once the final response is chosen. The goal is precise, idempotent ledger writes with minimal added latency and clear auditability for post-hoc billing reconciliations.
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
1) Ingest pipeline changes: add attempt_id, parent_request_id, route_priority, model_candidate_score, and attempt_outcome to the token-ingest envelope.
2) Attenuation algorithm: compute per-attempt allocation = base_token_count * attenuation_factor(route_priority, candidate_score, attempt_index). Default attenuation factors: primary route=1.0, fallback attempts exponentially decayed (0.5, 0.25...), simultaneous multi-model splits normalized to sum 1.0 across candidates.
3) Shard-level aggregator: keep small in-memory compact windows keyed by parent_request_id to produce a final reconciliation record once attempt_outcome==final.
4) Ledger writes: produce idempotent upserts to token_ledger with attempt_id and reconciliation_marker. Use s3-backed change-log for async retries.
5) Low-volume tenant sampling: for tenants with <1000 requests/day we apply sampled reconciliation to reduce overhead; sampling seed deterministically derived from tenant_id.
6) Backfill: a reconciliation worker (batch) will scan last 90 days to fix known duplicate Attributions produced during the incident INC-2025-07-11-token-duplicate.
7) Configuration: expose attenuation policy in console: route-level priority weight and a global attenuation profile per release.
Trade-offs and notes:
- We introduce additional metadata on the hot path; keep envelope additions compact (<=128 bytes) to avoid network pressure.
- Attenuation introduces slight opacity in raw logs; we add a reconciled flag and full provenance record to address audit requests.
- Sampling reduces accuracy for low-volume tenants but keeps cost bounded; product approved this for P2 customers only.
acceptance_criteria:
1) In staging, simulated multi-route requests (split, fallback, retry) show that summed ledger charge equals final reconciled allocation and no double-counting exceeds 0.1% across 100k test requests.
2) Production rollout for internal org: initial 10% tenant rollout shows no billing delta >0.5% for P1 customers and error rate on ledger writes remains <0.01%.
3) Dashboards populate per-request provenance for at least 14 days and reconciliation latency is <60s for 95th percentile.
4) Backfill job completes and corrects historical duplicates for at least the last 30 days in a dry-run, with audit report available.
5) Code review and security review completed and signed off by Security team.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for attenuation math including edge cases (zero tokens, concurrent splits, long retry chains). Integration test harness that replays production traffic traces with randomized route priorities. Staging canary: enable for 2 internal tenants and validate ledger writes with a canonical verifier. Load test: ensure ingest envelope size increase does not change p95 tail latency beyond 5ms for the ingest service under 95th percentile QPS.
QA checklist:
- deterministic sampling seeds validated
- idempotent upserts validated on duplicate attempt ingestion
- monitoring alerts smoke tested with synthetic anomalies
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 3% of tenants (internal/dev) for 48h. Verify reconciliation latency and ledger error rates.
Phase 2 (gradual): 25% of customers over 72h, enable backfill dry-run on older windows.
Phase 3: full rollout for P1 and P0 customers; P2/P3 following a week later with sampling behavior.
Rollback: toggle a feature-flag at the ingest-router that drops attenuation metadata and switches to legacy attribution path; backout window permitted up to 72h after rollout start.
Communication: post rollout summary to #billing-ops and notify finance and CS teams with reconciliation reports.
monitoring:
New dashboards:
- grafana: /d/billing/attenuated-allocs showing reconciliation_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), ledger_write_errors, duplication_rate_pre_vs_post.
- kafkametrics: attempt_envelope_size_hist, attempt_ingest_latency_ms.
Alerts:
- Reconciliation latency p95 > 60s for 15m -> paging to oncall.
- Ledger upsert failure rate > 0.1% for 10m -> page SRE.
- Duplication rate increase > 0.5% compared to baseline -> notify billing-eng and finance.
